facts.text: Bransford grew around the Chesapeake and Nashville Railroad, a 35‑mile line that linked Gallatin to Scottsville, making it a key stop before most of the track was abandoned.
The town sits in a valley of rolling hills and creek tributaries, where Bledsoe Creek’s headwaters flow through the center, shaping early farms and timber routes.
Pioneer settlers from Kentucky, including the Bledsoe brothers and Thomas Sharp Spencer, founded Bransford in the late 1700s, carving homesteads amid isolated wilderness.
Bransford’s elevation is 571 feet, and its coordinates are 36°30′15″N 86°16′12″W, placing it roughly 10 miles northeast of Gallatin and 42 miles northeast of Nashville.
